back: Observations of a variable recorded at successive (usually equal) intervals of time.
Trend (long-term direction), seasonal (repeats each year), cyclical (multi-year waves), irregular (one-off, unpredictable).
The mean of n consecutive values, recalculated as the window moves on one period; plotted at the middle of its periods.
Use the length of the seasonal cycle: 3 for termly, 4 for quarterly, 12 for monthly, 7 for daily data.
An even-order moving average falls between two periods; average consecutive pairs to line it up with a real period.
Seasonal deviation = actual value − trend value (moving average); average over years for each season.
Estimate = trend value (from the trend line) + average seasonal deviation for that season.
Moving averages remove seasonal and irregular variation so that the trend can be seen and described.
